subject: Different colours for bars in dodged bar chart?

messages.author: 87387836bb825314
messages.subject: Different colours for bars in dodged bar chart?
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to do a bar chart of the variables First and Last against
the categorical variable Basin. So far I've got it working with one or
other of First or Last, but I want both of them to come up next to
each other for each of the Basins. The added complexity is that I've
want different error bars for first and last.

What I've got at the moment is:

qplot(Basin, c(First, Last), data=mb, geom=c("bar", "errorbar"),
color=c("red", "blue"), ymax=c(First+FirstErr, Last+LastErr), ymin=c
(First-FirstErr, Last-LastErr), stat="identity", position="dodge")

That gives me both the first and the last next to each other, but
they're both the same colour. When I try and change the colour by
adding "colour = c("red", "blue") its the error bars that change
colour not the bars themselves.

What am I doing wrong here?

Cheers,

Robin

any legends for the colours, and I can't see any way to add them
manually. Is there another way that I should be doing this so I can
get a legend?

Robin

On Sun, Dec 06, 2009 at 11:22:34AM -0800, Robin Wilson wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I've worked out how to do this relatively simply: by using fill=c(I
> ("red"), I("blue")) in my call to qplot. However, this doesn't give me
> any legends for the colours, and I can't see any way to add them
> manually. Is there another way that I should be doing this so I can
> get a legend?

I always use the ggplot command. In this case the command is something
like


p <- ggplot(mtcars,aes(factor(cyl),gear,fill=factor(cyl)))+geom_bar(stat="identity")
p + scale_fill_manual("",values=c("4"="red","6"="blue","8"="black"))

Hope this helps,

Stefan
